$comment: last-release-sha is a ROOT option, not a per-package one. Nested inside packages['.'] it is
silently ignored - the schema's package object accepts unknown keys, so nothing complains and
release-please walks the whole inherited history anyway. Run 2 died with `other side closed`
part-way through backfilling it. Only the ROOT properties list carries this key.
It points at the 1.46.2 release commit, the parent of the extraction, so the changelog covers
this repository's own commits rather than 709 inherited compose-ai-tools ones.
The manifest seeds 1.46.2 - the LAST version already released under these coordinates, which is
what release-please reads it as. It is not the version to release next. The cutover commit is a
`feat!:`, so the first release cut here is 2.0.0: derived, not declared. Asserting 2.0.0 in the
manifest instead told release-please 2.0.0 was already out and to propose the NEXT one.
Re-basing had to go UP. 1.46.2 is on Central already, built from the compose-ai-tools tree these
modules were extracted from; restarting at 1.0.0 would rank below it and make `latest` resolve
to the stale upstream artifact. See docs/VERSIONING.md.
Versions here are INDEPENDENT of compose-ai-tools. That repository consumes these coordinates
at the version its gradle/libs.versions.toml pins; it no longer builds these modules.
$comment is the one key the schema rejects; everything else here validates against it.
